premise: Stegosaurus thinks his small, low head is no use — Triceratops has horns, Parasaurolophus a crest — but when the friends go looking for the softest new fern shoots, hidden low in the grass, his low head finds them first.
inspiration: Aesop's 'The Stag at the Pool' turned: the part he was shy of is the part that serves him best.
lesson: What makes you different can be just what is needed.
learning: Stegosaurus kept its head low and ate plants that grew near the ground.

en-US.title: Stegosaurus Finds the Best Shoots
en-US.text: {stegosaurus:enter} Stegosaurus always walked with his head down low, close to the grass. {stegosaurus:face sad} [sighs] "My head is so small," he said, "and so low." {triceratops:enter} Triceratops had three fine horns. {parasaurolophus:enter} Parasaurolophus had a long, curved crest. And Stegosaurus? Just a little head, down by his feet. {triceratops:face happy} One morning, Triceratops said, "Let's find the softest new fern shoots in the valley!" She looked with her head held high. {triceratops:live shake-head} "None here." Parasaurolophus looked from way up tall. She found some old fronds and {parasaurolophus:live munch} munched them. {parasaurolophus:face sad} "Too tough!" But Stegosaurus kept his head where it always was, down low. {stegosaurus:live sniff} {sfx:sniff} Sniff, sniff. And there, hidden in the grass, where only a low head would look, were tiny, curly, soft new shoots. {stegosaurus:face surprised} [excited] "Over here!" {triceratops:go to stegosaurus} {parasaurolophus:go to stegosaurus} His friends came running. {parasaurolophus:face happy} {triceratops:live munch} {sfx:munch} Munch, munch: the softest ever. [curious] "How did you find them?" asked Triceratops. {stegosaurus:face happy} {stegosaurus:live blush} Stegosaurus smiled shyly. "I was looking down here anyway."

es-ES.title: Los brotes más tiernos
es-ES.text: {stegosaurus:enter} Estegosaurio siempre caminaba con la cabeza gacha, pegadita a la hierba. {stegosaurus:face sad} [sighs] —Tengo la cabeza tan pequeña —decía—, y tan bajita… {triceratops:enter} Triceratops tenía tres cuernos preciosos. {parasaurolophus:enter} Parasaurolophus, una cresta larga y curva. ¿Y Estegosaurio? Solo una cabecita, allá abajo, junto a las patas. {triceratops:face happy} Una mañana, Triceratops dijo: —¡Vamos a buscar los brotes de helecho más tiernos del valle! Buscó con la cabeza bien alta. {triceratops:live shake-head} —Aquí no hay. Parasaurolophus buscó desde allá arriba. Encontró unas frondas viejas y {parasaurolophus:live munch} se puso a masticar. {parasaurolophus:face sad} —¡Durísimas! Pero Estegosaurio tenía la cabeza donde siempre, bien abajo. {stegosaurus:live sniff} {sfx:sniff} Snif, snif. Y allí, escondidos entre la hierba, donde solo mira una cabeza bajita, había brotes nuevos, chiquitines, enroscados y tiernos. {stegosaurus:face surprised} [excited] —¡Aquí, aquí! {triceratops:go to stegosaurus} {parasaurolophus:go to stegosaurus} Sus amigas llegaron corriendo. {parasaurolophus:face happy} {triceratops:live munch} {sfx:munch} Ñam, ñam: los más tiernos del mundo. [curious] —¿Cómo los has encontrado? —preguntó Triceratops. {stegosaurus:face happy} {stegosaurus:live blush} Estegosaurio sonrió, muy vergonzoso. —Es que yo ya miraba por aquí abajo.
